posts.name: Escher
posts.cooked:
Chaosmancer:

So Dark Psuedonym over on the Kickstarter just gave me a truly terrifying thought that I'd like to share with everyone… 

The only reason I could think of that ol' Smiling Jack couldn't be a Scion is because Gloomweaver "ate" him to make Skinwalker, and there might not be enough of him left to be turned into a Scion. Still, it was a fascinating idea that was scary enough I wanted to share it.

Is "Dark Psuedonym" my fleshchild duplicate?   (I'm Darth Pseudonym over on Kickstarter, and also on Steam, btw.)

I'm with you on the 'very worst person to become a scion' thing, but I don't know where you're getting the idea that Gloomy ate Jack's soul.  According to the Gloomweaver episode of Letters Page, they "switched places" when Gloomy inhabited the body to become the Skinwalker, and they never mentioned Spite again in that episode – which means Jack's soul got shoved off into the Realm of Discord somewhere, along with the majority of Gloomweaver's power (at least until Gloomypants was able to go into Rotting God form).

 

However, all that said, when I go back and read the Scion's Aid ARG fragment (which I haven't in six months), it sends me back to thinking it's gotta be Voss.  I know each of these points has counterarguments, but:

  1. The spoken lines sound more like something Voss would say than Spite. (In particular, "little heroes of Earth" sounds like an alien warlord.)

  2. The silhouette could certainly fit Voss (in a 'take a knee' pose), but would only fit Spite if he's in a particularly buff but not mutated state.

  3. Spite's soul was dumped into the Realm of Discord, which is weird and trippy but hardly 'beyond space and time', which is where the Scion says it was found.  But at 1:09 in the Gloomweaver Letters Page, that's precisely the phrase used to describe where Nightmist banishes her foes: "She's sending them nowhere.  She's sending them beyond space and time.  They are nowhere and nowhen." (Props to Chogb001, who noted this back in April, which helped me find the exact quote.)

 

I'd love to see Scion Spite, but the evidence for Voss is stronger.

Yes, Iron Legacy is one of the front-running candidates for the Tenth Scion.  The biggest argument against him is the Scion's Aid page from the ARG, which makes it clear that the Scion wants Oblivaeon's power for himself, which isn't really the Iron Legacy style.  Voss wants to rule the universe; Iron Legs wants justice at the cost of freedom.

I don't think so, mainly because time shenangins aren't exactly what Oblivaeon is known for.

 

We won't see any of the major forces from the RPG as Scions (as in if the team introduces a new immensley powerful villain, they won't have that villain have later become a scion for Oblivaeon) because the RPG timeline didn't exist until Oblivaeon was defeated and Oblivaeon can't act in times after he has been defeated.

 

Essentially, I don't think Oblivaeon is paradox proof like La Commodora, so since she was lost mid-fight with him, he didn't have the "time" to go and recruit her in his weakened state, and if he was going to do something like that, he would have gotten her ealier so she couldn't hit him that hard and add to his defeat.
